corpus: Book of Proverbs, World English Bible, selected sayings (public domain)
source_edition: The World English Bible (WEB): Proverbs, Project Gutenberg ebook 8247, release date June 1, 2005, most recently updated December 26, 2020. Text from www.ebible.org with slight reformatting by Martin Ward, as credited in the edition.
public_domain: The World English Bible is a public domain translation. The Project Gutenberg edition is public domain in the USA.

passages.question: What is the beginning of knowledge?
passages.answer: The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of knowledge; but the foolish despise wisdom and instruction.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What should a son do with his father's instruction and his mother's teaching?
passages.answer: My son, listen to your father's instruction, and don't forsake your mother's teaching: for they will be a garland to grace your head, and chains around your neck.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: How should you trust in Yahweh, and what should you not lean on?
passages.answer: Trust in Yahweh with all your heart, and don't lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What is supreme, and what should you get even if it costs all your possessions?
passages.answer: Wisdom is supreme. Get wisdom. Yes, though it costs all your possessions, get understanding.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: Where should the sluggard go, and whose ways should he consider?
passages.answer: Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise; which having no chief, overseer, or ruler, provides her bread in the summer, and gathers her food in the harvest.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: How many things does Yahweh hate, and what are the things that are an abomination to him?
passages.answer: There are six things which Yahweh hates; yes, seven which are an abomination to him: haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood; a heart that devises wicked schemes, feet that are swift in running to mischief, a false witness who utters lies, and he who sows discord among brothers.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What is the beginning of wisdom, and what is understanding?
passages.answer: The fear of Yahweh is the beginning of wisdom. The knowledge of the Holy One is understanding.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: Who becomes poor, and what does the hand of the diligent bring?
passages.answer: He becomes poor who works with a lazy hand, but the hand of the diligent brings wealth.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What does hatred stir up, and what does love cover?
passages.answer: Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all wrongs.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What is not lacking in the multitude of words, and who does wisely?
passages.answer: In the multitude of words there is no lack of disobedience, but he who restrains his lips does wisely.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What is an abomination to Yahweh, and what is his delight?
passages.answer: A false balance is an abomination to Yahweh, but accurate weights are his delight.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What comes when pride comes, and what comes with humility?
passages.answer: When pride comes, then comes shame, but with humility comes wisdom.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What weighs down a man's heart, and what makes it glad?
passages.answer: Anxiety in a man's heart weighs it down, but a kind word makes it glad.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: Who grows wise, and who suffers harm?
passages.answer: One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What turns away wrath, and what stirs up anger?
passages.answer: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What happens to plans where there is no counsel, and how are plans established?
passages.answer: Where there is no counsel, plans fail; but in a multitude of counselors they are established.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What goes before destruction, and what goes before a fall?
passages.answer: Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: Who is better than the mighty, and who is better than one who takes a city?
passages.answer: One who is slow to anger is better than the mighty; one who rules his spirit, than he who takes a city.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: When does a friend love, and what is a brother born for?
passages.answer: A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What is the name of Yahweh like, and who runs to it?
passages.answer: The name of Yahweh is a strong tower: the righteous run to him, and are safe.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: Who lends to Yahweh, and what will Yahweh do for him?
passages.answer: He who has pity on the poor lends to Yahweh; he will reward him.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What is more acceptable to Yahweh than sacrifice?
passages.answer: To do righteousness and justice is more acceptable to Yahweh than sacrifice.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: Why should you not exploit the poor or crush the needy in court?
passages.answer: Don't exploit the poor, because he is poor; and don't crush the needy in court; for Yahweh will plead their case, and plunder the life of those who plunder them.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has strife? Who has complaints? Who has needless bruises? Who has bloodshot eyes?
passages.answer: Those who stay long at the wine; those who go to seek out mixed wine.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What is a word fitly spoken like?
passages.answer: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What sharpens iron, and what does a man sharpen?
passages.answer: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend's countenance.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: Who does not prosper, and who finds mercy?
passages.answer: He who conceals his sins doesn't prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them finds mercy.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What things are never satisfied, and what things do not say Enough?
passages.answer: "The leach has two daughters: 'Give, give.' "There are three things that are never satisfied; four that don't say, 'Enough:' Sheol, the barren womb; the earth that is not satisfied with water; and the fire that doesn't say, 'Enough.'
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)

passages.question: What four things are little on the earth but exceedingly wise?
passages.answer: "There are four things which are little on the earth, but they are exceedingly wise: the ants are not a strong people, yet they provide their food in the summer. The conies are but a feeble folk, yet make they their houses in the rocks. The locusts have no king, yet they advance in ranks. You can catch a lizard with your hands, yet it is in kings' palaces.
passages.source: World English Bible, Book of Proverbs (Project Gutenberg 8247)
